coreSettings.reasoning: Personal preference, I think 500ms is way too long for fading elements.

There's a lot of personal preference here. For example, I prefer NPCs to also have Vision Enabled on, since it lets me parse what a specific enemy is able to see at any given moment. Importantly I'd advice against having Ring Enabled On even if you're using Dynamic Rings for everything -- it will interfere with some Summons automations, like Wall of Stone.
Frankly I just think that it looks really bad. And there are other ways to display damage numbers.

systemSettings.reasoning: Enabled since I tend to run games RAW.

I don't mind playing looting corpses at a 'distance', since it's assumed they walk around during the short break. But loot actors should be directly interacted with, as there might be a trap nearby :)
Makes players actually see the HUD's clock above the chat.
On by default, turned off in scene configs for indoor scenes and whatnot.

modules.name: Big Bad Module Manager
modules.note: Currently the best solution for managing modules, their settings, and syncing settings with users.

settings.reasoning: Optional, but makes it easier to organize modules.

path: Prompt to enable newly installed modules
settings.reasoning: Personally I found it annoying.

modules.name: Dice So Nice!
modules.note: The only thing stopping me from declaring Dice So Nice as Essential is the fact that it can cause some synchronicity issues and potential performance problems. Otherwise, it's the best solution to have 3d dice on the table.

settings.reasoning: Players having different animation speeds can cause sync issues -- some players will see the result before others, and it can be jarring. This doesn't solve it (since it's still possible for players to turn off the 3D dice client-side), but it helps mitigate it. Consider 3x if the dice rolls still take too long.
Personal preference -- when playing the enemies' turns I prefer to keep things quick.

path: Show Ghost dice for hidden rolls
settings.to: For player rolls only (hide GM rolls)
settings.reasoning: Ghost dice are fun to see, but if the players see the GM make secret checks they might start metagaming unintentionally.

modules.name: Quick Insert - Search Widget
modules.note: I am honestly tempted to say that this is the single best module for Foundry. Lightning-fast and just so convenient, I cannot imagine using Foundry without it. Has a bunch of customization settings, though I am more than happy with the defaults.

modules.name: Bar Brawl
modules.note: Out of the box it's already better than Foundry's own resource bars, offering more customisation. With some setup you can make tons of cool effects andn use custom images for bars.

settings.reasoning: There are a lot of settings you could be changing, so I'm not providing specifics. Personally I like to show the NPCs percentage health and the player characters actual numbers, and I use custom pixel-art health bars in place of the generic Foundry gradient ones.

modules.name: PF2e Secrets of Grayce
modules.note: Pathfinder's newest beginner box. The intro is more or less of the same quality, maybe a bit better (less nonsensical story-wise). The follow-up adventures are way, way better than Troubles in Otari.

modules.name: ✋ Raise My Hand
modules.note: Very simple module that allows players to press H to 'raise their hand', indicating to the GM that they want to say something. The inclusion of the X-Card makes it Essential in my eyes.

settings.reasoning: Personal preference, I find it much harder to miss with the UI notification enabled.
Preference, but you can't miss a middle-of-the-screen popup.

modules.name: Alternative Pause Icon
modules.note: A bunch of ways to edit the default pause overlay.

settings.reasoning: This and everything else here is personal preference. Move it out of the way so it doesn't obstruct the view of the scene.
One rotation a minute.
Less annoying.
I simply remove it, the icon should be enough in my opinion.

modules.name: socketlib
modules.note: An oft-used dependency that allows other modules to execute things as GM/player.

modules.name: Break Time
modules.note: A module to 'automate' taking breaks, allowing players to mark when they're back. Also has afk/back functionality built in.

settings.reasoning: This will depend on how long your breaks are.

modules.name: Cautious Gamemaster's Pack
modules.note: A number of useful small settings, exactly what it says on the tin.

settings.reasoning: Incredibly mild, but allows the GM to send items/actions in chat without it being flagged is done by the character.

path: Blind rolls made by hidden tokens
settings.reasoning: Good failsafe in case you forget to set a sneak/perception check on an enemy to blind beforehand.

modules.name: libWrapper
modules.note: A module to detect and prevent potential module conflicts.

modules.name: Remote Highlight UI
modules.note: A quick and easy way to point out things on the screen so the players know what they need to click.

modules.name: Z Scatter
modules.note: Slightly displaces tokens if two of the same size are in one square. Massively helps whenever verticality is involved.

settings.reasoning: One of the main uses cases for me is when one token is directly above another, so this is essential.
It's already possible to see tokens of different sizes over each other, so this is not necessary.
Preference. I find it that 0.15 dislodges the tokens enough to be easily selectable, but still clearly indicates which square they're in.

modules.name: Find the Culprit!
modules.note: A utility to test your module setup if something goes wrong. I can't say it always works out, but it can still be very helpful.

modules.name: Enhanced Audio Resources [Testing]
modules.note: This module is new to me, but it does make the playlist controls much better. While it's clearly vibe-coded, it seems quite functional so far in my testing.

modules.name: PF2e Flip Token / Foundry Flip Token
modules.note: This is analogues to the premium Token Flip module, with fewer options but similar results. It's a little janky, but if you need a way to constantly swap between two token images, this is easier than playing with rule elements.

modules.name: Sequencer
modules.note: This is what's powering pretty much every single animation module on Foundry. Besides being required for all those other modules, it's a powerful tool in its own right if you want to wrap your hand around it.

modules.name: Boss Bar
modules.note: Big full-screen health bar for the boss enemies, with a satisfying hit animation. Has a way to make your own designs as well!

modules.name: Custom CSS
modules.note: If you are at a midpoint where you understand CSS and want to do some tweaks to Foundry's visuals, but do not want to build your own module, Custom CSS will do the job. I personally used it to re-style the journals for one of my campaigns, and it worked well enough.

modules.name: Eskie Effects Free
modules.note: Highly recommend this pack, lots of beautiful effects. They are on a more abstract side than, say, JB2A, somewhat reminiscent of JRPGs in my mind. And I, frankly, much prefer that. Highly recommend the premium as well.

modules.name: Eskie Effects
modules.note: Full package of the great effects. Highly recommended.

modules.name: Eskie Macro Pack
modules.note: Premade macros that play specific animations. Most of them rely on the full version, not the free one, and will fail if you don't have it. They also rely on some additional dependencies. If you choose to use this pack, you can integrate the macros into whatever pipeline you're using, I wouldn't recommend activating them 'by hand'. It's also a great source to pick up how to hand-write Sequences if you want to make your own specific animations that go beyond Trigger Animations' reach.

modules.name: Foundry Summons
modules.note: A module to create a controlled copy of any actor in the compendia. Technically it's functional right out of the box, but unrestricted. PF2e Summons Helper is what uses it for specific spells and effects.

settings.reasoning: Unless your players are actively trying to sabotage the game, there shouldn't be an issue with them using Foundry Summons.
Allows the users to check out the statblock of whatever they're about to summon. This can lead to metagaming, but once again, it's a player issue, not a module issue.

modules.name: Transient Compendium Actor Library
modules.note: A way for all the summoning tools to have real actors without flooding the actors tab.

modules.name: Gambit's FXMaster
modules.note: At the minimum this can be used for some cool weather particle effects. More available in the premium version. The ceiling is quite high if you want to tinker with the custom settings.

modules.name: Gambit's FXMaster+
modules.note: More effects than the free version.

modules.name: JB2A - Jules&Ben's Animated Assets
modules.note: So many things straight up require this that I might as well classify it as a dependency. Most modules won't ask you for the premium version, free is enough.

modules.name: JB2A - Patreon Complete Collection
modules.note: This isn't really required, like the free version is, but it offers a ton of options and variants. I'd very much recommend subscribing, if even once, to get a pack and use it if you want more home-made animations. Premade animation packs usually do not rely on premium assets, unsurprisingly.

modules.name: BLFX Assets | Pack-01
modules.note: Personally, I don't use the animation editor itself. It's just not good enough for my PF2e needs, so far as there's no option to change the auto-recognition. But the assets are a decent bit of extra stuff if you feel like JB2A and Eskie are not covering everything you want to animate.

modules.name: Genga: System Agnostic Anime Animations
modules.note: The animations themselves are not for me, as they are way too meta, but it serves as a dependency for a different module.

modules.name: Token Magic FX
modules.note: Various effects applicable to the token images, including both static and animated. It's nice, even though my experience of using it with dynamic tokens have been mixed (because the dynamic tokens I make tend to have a lot of extra padding). It's required for at least some modules here, and it can be used separately to apply token and template effects.

settings.reasoning: Not a fan at all. They stretch wierdly, don't match the shapes for circles, and generally look kinda iffy. The functionality itself is great, it's just the presets that are lacking. Genga will prompt you to disable it on startup.

modules.name: Pathfinder Tokens: Monster Core
modules.note: It saves time, especially if you're not comfortable making pop-out tokens yourself. The artwork is all available online (not on Nethys anymore, but Demiplane still has it), so it's really just convenience.

modules.name: Pathfinder Tokens: Monster Core 2
modules.note: Same reasoning as Monster Core 1, saves you time. Has some art not on the Demiplane, presumably?

modules.name: Pathfinder Tokens: NPC Core
modules.note: Same as Monster Core, but for NPCs. I do find this one a little bit more useful, because it's such a common occurance to need a token for a bystander of some sorts. It's nice to have a proverbial commoner or innkeeper at the ready.

modules.name: Pathfinder Tokens: Bestiaries
modules.note: These are the ones from premaster times. A lot of these are covered by Monster Core and Monster Core 2. Some artworks were changed though, so if you have both you might have more options. Very low priority, but not useless even in remaster days.

modules.name: Pathfinder Tokens: Myth and Magic
modules.note: Same treatment as the main line modules for tokens from a variety of sources. I'd actually argue that these might be more useful than the Core ones, because you can stumble upon some really cool artwork that you likely wouldn't have found otherwise by just searching for an 'Ogre Warrior' or whatnot. Doubly so if you also have the character gallery.

modules.name: Pathfinder Tokens: Draconic Codex
modules.note: Latest at the time of writing. I think it overlaps a bit with the Core modules, but it does have all of the new shiny dragons from the Draconic Codex.

modules.name: Pathfinder Tokens: Character Gallery
modules.note: If you're wondering which token pack to buy, I would actually highly suggest this over anything else. Huge variety of artwork, but the important part is the gallery itself -- you can filter for specific things and then just drag-and-drop onto an existing actor. You don't really _need_ a goblin warrior token from the Monster Core if you can just look up _a_ goblin whose look you like and assign that artwork to the actor which is already shipped as part of PF2e system. And if you get more modules with art, the Character Gallery picks them up as well. Highly recommended.

modules.name: PF2e Apparatus
modules.note: At the time of writing, this is not released. Appratus is my own module, with the goal of automating not just specific actions, but the flow of combat as well. In my eyes, clicking a 'Vicious Swing' should visibly cost 2 actions, prompt the user for a target, resolve an attack, roll the damage (if hit) with the bonus dice included. This is not the typical style of play and this module will not be for everyone, but it's how I see the automation on Foundry play out for myself. At least in a game as well-supported as PF2e. I will not be beating the 'video-game' allegations.

modules.name: PF2e Afflictioner
modules.note: While it's, frankly, a mess, and has a lot of bugs no matter what I try to do with it, ultimately it's still the best way to track afflictions. By a mile. Just be sure to not leave it all to the automation and keep an eye on the manual management.

settings.reasoning: Like it says on the tin, allows for rerolls. Also useful in case someone forgot to apply some sort of bonus or penalty.

This is _probably_ RAW. The problem is, both this being false and true I'm still experiencing desyncs from time to time. I am not sure what's causing them, but you might need to mannually do things either way.

modules.name: PF2e Alchemist Remaster Duct Tape
modules.note: What a fantastic module. While the baseline Quick Alchemy is very good now, this adds some extra QoL for alchemists. The only reason you wouldn't want this module is if there are no alchemists in the party. And even then it works with Wandering Chefs, Munitions Crafter, and archetypes.

modules.name: PF2e Avatars
modules.note: I haven't tested it thoroughly, but from what I've seen I'm very impressed. Automated battle forms, and it even grabs relevant pictures if you have the token modules. One just doesn't get many opportunities to test how robust a rank 10 spell automation is.

modules.name: PF2e Avatars
modules.note: I haven't tested it thoroughly, but from what I've seen I'm very impressed. Automated battle forms, and it even grabs relevant pictures if you have the token modules. One just doesn't get many opportunities to test how robust a rank 10 spell automation is.

modules.name: PF2e Avoid Notice
modules.note: On its own, it compared the stealth check of allied who try to Avoid Notice with the Perception of enemies. When paired with Visioner, it automates the process. I'd say that this module is always worth it, Visioner is another story.

settings.reasoning: Personal preference.

path: Toggle on GM-Hidden combatants at  Combat Start
settings.reasoning: Safe to use with another layer of automation. Ensures you're not accidentally moving hidden tokens around. You might want to NOT use it if you don't use Visioner.
I am using other automations for this exploration activity.

modules.name: PF2e Visioner
modules.note: I am on the fence about Visioner. On one hand, it supposedly automates the thing that is incredibly annoying to even try to track without it. On another, it's a massive performance hit, and it constantly runs into issues. In recent versions I ran into bugs that really slowed things down, but supposedly that should be fixed now. For now I'll keep using it and I can tentatively recommend it for the good it does.

path: Require GM Approval for Door Peek
settings.reasoning: Safety precaution. I also suggest you check the keybinding to set them as you like, and sync that with your players.

modules.name: PF2e Creature Sounds
modules.note: I'd say it's not for everyone, but I find it nice to have some extra sounds here and there. Some of them are a bit on the 'funni' side though, and the variety is limited. If you're willing to go the extra mile and do your own sound sets, this is by far the best way to do it, though.

settings.reasoning: Preference, match to the comfort level. Keep in mind that this is a client-side setting and you might want to let your players know that they can change it.

modules.name: PF2e Companion Compendia
modules.note: It's kinda wild that there's still nothing for it in core in the big 2026. This module is basically a requirement if any of your players have any animal companions, eidolon, or followers, or whatever else.

settings.reasoning: Preference, match to the comfort level. Keep in mind that this is a client-side setting and you might want to let your players know that they can change it.

modules.name: PF2e Workbench
modules.note: Well, it's the workbench. A treasure trove of useful settings, really. Pretty much just a direct extension of the baseline PF2e System.

path: Mystify alchemical and magical items on npcs, if the PF2e system setting NPCs are lootable is enabled.
to: Mystify items on npc reaching 0 hp
settings.reasoning: This makes the gear on enemies readable as a GM, but mystifies it when they fall.

path: Use party level as base for per-rarity thresholds
settings.reasoning: I like to set it so the party auto-identifies items that are lower level than them.

This makes it so if the party is level 12, and an item is level 11 or lower, it will remain revealed. You can also set it for other rarities, I have Uncommon at PL-1, Rare at PL-2, and Unique at PL-4.
I believe that it's usually better to have your players learn to target things to speed up combat. You can also set it to cancel an untargeted attack instead.
Reminds people about Slowed, Stunned, and Quickened.

This is great. Except that it's broken. RAW, a roll of a 1 on the recharge means that the ability will be unavailable for a WHOLE round. So if a creature breathes on round 3, gets 1 on recharge, they'll be able to breathe on round 5, not 4. In Workbench implementation, it's one less than intended. I plan on opening an issue about it.
Keep 'em guessing.
There's so much functionality to this that it could've been its own module. It's awesome. Configure the rest as you like.
Nice little utility to bring NPCs to specific levels, preserving their proficiency in aspects.

Find it at the bottom of the journal tab. Basically it allows you to improvise rolls. Imagine you suddenly need a level 4 baker to perform their Crafting check, and you consider them Extreme at what they do. Without needing to look up GM tables, you can go to NPC roller -> Skills -> Level 4 Extreme and have your result at the ready (or set the DC to be 10+that number).

path: Ctrl-click Cast to cast in private
settings.reasoning: This suite of configs is a great way to mistify spells while letting people still interact with them.

path: ... and list the party members that know the autorevealed spell

settings.reasoning: Sets it as default.

path: Post public message that a spell has been cast.
settings.reasoning: And this lets players still perform saves if needed or try to recognize a spell.

path: ... and show the public message to the gm also.
... and show spell traits in the public message.
... but exclude these traits from the public message
Show feat names in rarity colour on actor sheets.
settings.reasoning: This and the next 3 settings are just cosmetic. I like the way they look.

path: Setting initiative to just before the current combatant
settings.reasoning: This and almost everything after in this category is almost pure automation. I don't see a reason to not have it on.

path: ... and automatically roll recovery after that.
Automatically apply persistent healing rolled by the system.
Automatically reduce stunned on turn start
Automatically give unconscious if Dying removed at 0 HP.
Automatically remove unconscious if healed to greater than 0 HP.
Automatically give Wounded when Dying is removed
... depending on if last damage was nonlethal.
... and add one more dying if critically damaged by an enemy.
... and add additional dying level(s) if taking damage when dying.
Automatically remove Dying when healed to above 0 HP.
Characters automatically drop held items on becoming unconscious.
Automatically decrease the frightened condition each turn.

modules.name: Trigger Engine
modules.note: For a while now Trigger has been the new big name on the block for Foundry Automation. It's a set of tools to set up sequences of interaction with the Foundry's 'insides', and the sky's the limit, especially if you're comfortable with macros. The Trigger Trove has some PF2e automations and is still being updated.

settings.reasoning: This will depend on whether you use any other automation modules. For example, I don't have the Dying & Wounded enabled, because for now I prefer the Workshop implementation. This might change in the future though.

modules.name: Trigger Trove
modules.note: If you're using Trigger Engine, I highly recommend installing this. Both because it's a set of good automations, but also because these are great illustrations for how you can make your own.

modules.name: Phil's PF2e Action Colours 🚥
modules.note: Seems to generally work better than Wayfinder. Still not perfect, but that's just system complexity issues.

settings.reasoning: Helps prevent players from getting stuck at walls. I'd advise on keeping it 'Only in Combat', since otherwise it's possible to 'feel' through fog of war, even unintenionally. But it's, ultimately, preference.
Settings here are almost entirely preference. I like the idea of showing the pathing to other players, since it helps them figure out where someone might've went.

modules.name: PSFX - Peri's Sound Effects
modules.note: I treat the free version of this as a dependency, since there are at least a couple of things that use it, or used to use it. Might as well have it around.

modules.name: PSFX - Ambience
modules.note: One of three paid PSFX modules. Do you need sounds? You can have sounds. There's only a couple of them though.

modules.name: PSFX - Music
modules.note: Another of the three. It's not very populated at the moment, but the tracks sound nice.

modules.name: PSFX - Patreon
modules.note: Expanded version of the free stuff. Get it for more sound effects if you want to play around with that. IMPORTANT: Disable the free module if you do. Sequencer gets confused otherwise and you'll run into errors. Unlike JB2A, Sequencer cannot combine the free and paid versions into one shared database.

modules.name: PF2e Bard Helper
modules.note: Like with the Alchemist Duct Tape, the only reason you wouldn't want this is if there are no bards in your party. It does a great job of maintaining the effects and spells RAW.

modules.name: PF2e Dailies
modules.note: Adds a button to the character sheet to automate a lot of daily preparations, such as staves, commander tactics, familiar abilities. You can even add your own!

modules.name: PF2e Effect Halo
modules.note: Gotta give it the 'essential' rating, seeing how many effects a character can have in PF2e and how awful they look in the core system.

modules.name: pf2E Extempore Effects
modules.note: Try as you might to automate everything, you will run into missing bits and pieces everywhere. Extempore is a way to apply basically the text of a chat message to a token. It parses some text, such as duration, automatically.

settings.reasoning: Never felt necessary to me, but it's a preference.

path: Shorten 'Stage 2' to e.g. '[2/6]' in effect badges
settings.reasoning: Personal preference.

modules.name: PF2e Eidolon Helper
modules.note: Number three of the 'required' modules if you've got a certain class in your game. The usage might not be obvious -- you will need to link a summoner and their eidolon with a macro.

settings.reasoning: All of these settings are RAW. All of them seem functional. So just enable everything.

modules.name: pF2e See Simple Scale Statistics
modules.note: This is a very simple utility that lets you see how a creature's stats compare to its level. For example you can see if the creature has average, high, or extreme AC for its level. It will also warn you if something is 'off' about a creature, like having too many weak stats or vice versa.

modules.name: PF2e Specific Familiars
modules.note: Cousin-compendium to PF2e Creature Compendia, adding the abilities for the 'specific familiars'. No reason not to use.

modules.name: Pf2E Modifiers Matter
modules.note: I am incredibly close to declaring this as essential purely because of how relevant it is to discussions around PF2e and players' understanding of the system. Seeing constant highlights of what exactly contributed to a roll does wonders.

path: Ignore Crit Fail over Fail on attacks
settings.reasoning: Unless your party's got a swashbuckler, then you might as well have it on.

modules.name: SETT: Some Extra Token (ring) Types
modules.note: This adds some more dynamic rings, but the main benefit is being able to add your own! If you figure out how to make them, SETT will handle making them interactable on Foundry.

modules.name: REDY: Reactive Dynamic Token Rings
modules.note: This is a dependency for SETT, and it has some cute features of its own. It can flash the dynamic ring in colors, such as when creatures take damage or are healed.

settings.reasoning: This and the other settings here are purely cosmetic and personal preference. Experiment and see what you like.
Personal preference, I don't like condition flashing.

modules.name: PF2e Summons Assistant
modules.note: This helps out SO MUCH I'm putting it into the Essential category. A ton of automations, and full usability of any 'Summon' spells.

modules.name: PF2e Brewrata
modules.note: Used by the Summons Assistant. I am not entirely sure about using it on its own for now, but there is potential here.

modules.name: Pf2e Sustain Reminder
modules.note: Used by the Summons Assistant. And it's still good on its own -- it creates a reminder effect for spells you're sustaining, and drops a chat card when your turn begins.

modules.name: Library: Item Select Dialog
modules.note: Used by the Kineticist Companion. No harm in having it.

modules.name: Portal
modules.note: Used by the Kineticist Companion. No harm in having it.

modules.name: PF2e Kineticist's Companion
modules.note: Some nice things for a couple of Kineticist abilities. Keep in mind that Thermal Nimbus is also automated by Trigger Engine, so you'll need to disable it there (Kineticist Companion does not have a way to disable an automation, unfortunately).

modules.name: TokenMagic Automatic Wounds
modules.note: I had no idea this token existed until recently, having been doing a similar thing by hand. It seems pretty nice, though I would appreciate if there was an option for it to not work for certain traits, like Construct or Ooze. It's possible to manually change the blood type and disable it work specific tokens though (check the Macros for that).

modules.name: PF2e Aztec's Inline Builder
modules.note: This is purely a utility to construct an inline PF2e thing quickly. Saves time if you're fully making your own adventures, hazards, and whatnot.

modules.name: PF2e Usage Updater
modules.note: Does exactly what it says on the tin -- checks the time having passed for things with cooldown and updates them accordingly. So if someone uses a 1/hour ability, it will be available again after an hour passes in game time.

settings.reasoning: I like the automation, and it's a popular item.
Not sure why it wouldn't be enabled, it shouldn't be an issue for players to see the cooldown of their abilities.
In case you want to look up how long exactly until an action is refreshed.

modules.name: PF2e Item Activations
modules.note: Really nice module that adds actions embedded into items in the character's inventory. For example, if a character gets the 'Bracelets of Dashing', they'll also find the 'Jangling Dash' action on their character sheet, with proper cooldown tracking and all. Additionally, the actions are generated by parsing text, so it will work even with the homebrew items you make!

modules.name: Sundry. Small Tidbits for (Mostly) PF2e
modules.note: This is basically a bunch of small fixes in one module, which is nice.

settings.reasoning: Makes the chat messages a little bit more distinct.

path: Item Property Runes on Actor Sheet

settings.reasoning: It's a cute idea. Unfortunately it doesn't quite work. A non-identified item is distinct by lacking a value and an edit button, so any player can clearly see what it really is. If they are able to suspend disbelief, it's just a shortcut for the GMs to not bother with swapping out items entirely.
Much better, otherwise the headers of actors get completely flooded from all the things injected into them.
Prone is a very common condition, and it's nice to have a distinct visual effect to it.
You can set up a journal with loading tips, to remind people that they should be striking at -10 MAP, as Valeros intended.

path: PF2e Toolbelt - Target Helper Unrolled Roll
settings.reasoning: Makes the roll button stand out a bit more.
This is new to me, but it seems pretty fun. Let's fate decide the direction of some abilities and whatnot.

Now, an important note -- I don't actually use this setting anymore. I switched to tracking reactions my own way. But it's in a home module that I'm not releasing publicly yet, and the Sundry implementation covers most of what you might need.

modules.name: PF2e HUD
modules.note: I will boldly proclaim PF2e HUD to be essential. The amount of utility it brings, along with how neatly arranged everything is just can't be beat. Plus, it has an incredibly level of customization, so you can keep exactly the parts you want.

settings.reasoning: I show my players enemies' health bars, just without the actual numerical value, so the health status is redundant for my needs. I still have it configured to just show whether someone is above or below 50% health just in case.
Doesn't seem necessary at all.
Shows the actual numerical HP for player characters.
Please note that this is only for myself, the GM. For players, I keep it soft-locked at 'Manual Selection'.
Preference. And this is a client side thing, so players can select their own.
I don't really like the Token HUD here, it's a bit bloated and really big. But you may choose to keep it around.

modules.name: PF2E HUD Colors
modules.note: If there is one criticism of HUD I have is that it's very gray-looking. This fixes it, and the colours are really well-selected.

modules.name: Trigger Animations
modules.note: If you've been around for a while, you might remember PF2e Graphics, which never got updated for V13 properly. THIS is its 'spiritual successor', wired to work in the same framework as Trigger Animations. It has a steeper learning curve than Automated Animations or even the BLFX Animation Editor, but I'd still suggest going with it. Even if you don't want to learn how to make your own animations, the trove of them is constantly being updated.

modules.name: Trigger Animation Trove (PF2e / SF2e)
modules.note: This is a collection of ready-made animations for PF2e using Trigger Animations. Note that it's built around the patreon version of JB2A. Some animations have workarounds.

modules.name: GGG: Sequencer Sound DB Collection
modules.note: Used by Trigger Animation Trove in place of PSFX.

modules.name: Prime Performance
modules.note: Haven't used it before, currently trying it out to see if anything goes wrong.

modules.name: PF2e Ranged Combat
modules.note: Since ammo has been added to the core PF2e itself, it's been rough with the module. In core, enemies don't expend ammo automatically. With this module installed, they expend double ammo on each shot -- but only for no reload weapons. If you use the NPC configurator, you can fix it, assigning the weapons correctly and it will only consume 1 ammo. I am, frankly, on the fence about this one, and I am not sure I will continue using it for the time being. FOr the time being, I will try and update this document with my findings.

modules.name: PF2e Utility Buttons
modules.note: I prefer Utility Buttons over PF2e Flat Check because it doesn't split into a separate message and can be rerolled. It does have a habit of attaching an effect to _everything_ an actor does, but it's not that big of a deal.

modules.name: PF2e Subsystems
modules.note: This is basically a frontend UI for Influence, Research, Chases, and Infiltrations. It sticks to RAW and presents them to players in a distinct UI.

modules.name: PF2e Subsystem Theming
modules.note: Required for Subsystems and Bestiary. You can also set up your own custom themes within.

modules.name: PF2e Bestiary Tracking
modules.note: This lets players keep track of enemies, NPCs, and hazards they've encountered. The specifics and settings are highly up to you and your GMing style.

modules.name: Battlezoo: Eldamon for Pathfinder 2e | Roll For Combat
modules.note: It's just like that one obscure Nintendo franchise! This is definitely not everyone's cup of tea, and it clashes startkly with PF2e. But I would say that the Elemental Avatar slots in very nicely into PF2e as-is. The Eldamon barely comes up, so you're just playing an alternative Kineticist with 13 various elements.

modules.name: Battlezoo Ancestries: Dragons for PF2e by Roll for Combat
modules.note: Adds the dragon ancestry. Not 'dragonborn', or 'dragonblood', or whatever else, straight up just dragon. The explanation is incredibly thin, but if someone really wants to play a dragon, this is the way.

modules.name: Battlezoo Ancestries: Dragons for PF2e by Roll for Combat
modules.note: Adds the dragon ancestry. Not 'dragonborn', or 'dragonblood', or whatever else, straight up just dragon. The explanation is incredibly thin, but if someone really wants to play a dragon, this is the way.

modules.name: Battlezoo Jewel of the Indigo Isles for PF2e | Roll For Combat
modules.note: Pirate-adjacent adventure path (levels 1-11), set in a world distinct from Golarion. Very whimsical and colorful. It does come with some player options, but I'd still say it's primarily GM content.

modules.name: Battlezoo — World of Battlezoo: Indigo Isles for Pathfinder 2e
modules.note: Think of this like 'Lost Omens: Indigo Isles', if it was mainline. Basically a book with both GM hooks, NPCs, and player options, all related to the setting. Obvious tie-in to the adventure itself.

modules.name: Battlezoo Bestiary for PF2e by Roll For Combat
modules.note: That's one nice way to throw some curveballs at your players expecting familiar stat blocks. Once again, it does include SOME player content, but it's definitely not that focus.

modules.name: Universal Battlemap Importer
modules.note: I don't have a lot of experience with it, but it's for importing battlemaps, obviously enough.

modules.name: PF2e RPG Numbers & More
modules.note: It adds bells and whistles to things, like showing action results, damage dealt, and the like. I'd suggest you set it up to your liking, since all of it is purely taste-based.

modules.name: Rideable
modules.note: I have to admit I'm not exactly a fan of Rideable, but maybe I'm doing something wrong. It bugged out for me in a number of different ways over my time running games. And I'm not too happy that it relies on an unmaintained library. But if you've got a player using a mount, there's kinda-sorta no way around it.

modules.note: Toolbelt adds so much that I can't place it as anything lower than Essential. It's basically Workbench 2 in my eyes.
